summary: Evening reserved-pool throughput collapse correlated with GPU page-faults and autoscaler hysteresis
description:
Issue summary:
Between 18:10-19:05 PDT on 2026-03-12, QuillEdge reported sustained throughput collapse on their reserved capacity pool (P50 and P95 tokens/s dropped by ~65%). Customers experienced increased queueing and elevated p99 latency for short-lived streaming requests.

Impact:
- Customer production workloads degraded for ~55 minutes during evening traffic ramp.
- Automated fallbacks to hosted routes triggered for some requests.
- No data loss; inference responses were delayed or routed to lower-capacity fallbacks.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2 (cluster id: rp-west-22).
- Customer model pin: redwood-instruct-7b-v2, concurrency config: 12 per slot.

Timeline (high-level):
- 18:08: first alerts — increased queue length and attach latencies.
- 18:12: customer open ticket with support; observed p99 spikes.
- 18:20: platform metrics showed repeated GPU PGFAULT events on 3 nodes in pool.
- 18:25: autoscaler reacted by shrinking pool (hysteresis window causing several slot drains).
- 18:30-19:00: throughput remained depressed while evicted slots cycled and KV cache warmups repeated.
- 19:02: mitigation rollout (driver patch + autoscaler threshold tweak) applied to pool.
- 19:05: observed recovery to baseline.

Steps to reproduce (internal repro notes):
1. Seed reserved pool with mixed short-lived streaming client (avg token length 50) and background prefetch batchers.
2. Induce sudden increase of small-stream connections (~3x baseline) over 2 minutes.
3. Force a simulated GPU driver memory pressure to produce page fault spikes (test harness only).
4. Observe autoscaler decision path under current hysteresis (cooldown 90s) and slot drain behavior.

Observed metrics & logs (high level):
- GPU PGFAULT count: nodes gpu-ww-004/006/009 ~120-220 faults in 10m window.
- Kernel OOM/eviction logs: repeated TDR-like driver resets reported but driver recovered without full node reboot.
- Autoscaler actions: 3 slot shrinks starting 18:24, completed by 18:28.
- KV cache miss rate spiked from 4% to 42% during slot churn.
- Request fallback/incidence: ~1.8% routed to hosted fallback for some tenants.

Hypothesis:
Primary cause is transient GPU memory pressure that manifested as driver-level page-faults on a subset of GPUs serving QuillEdge. The autoscaler interpreted the degraded attach/heartbeat signals and initiated scale-downs due to conservative hysteresis thresholds. The resulting slot churn forced repeated KV cache rebuilds and increased per-request cold cost and latency, compounding the throughput collapse. We also observed that a background snapshotter process on the same nodes increased NVMe IO, amplifying driver latency under the small-stream-dominated workload.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced elevated PGFAULT counts on staging when running mixed small-stream + snapshotter IO.
- Driver logs indicate late-page reclamation stalls prior to recoveries (no fatal crashes).
- Autoscaler logic currently uses attach-latency + heartbeat-drop windows (90s cooldown) which, combined with immediate reactive shrink, created a feedback loop.
- KV cache warmup time for these models is non-trivial and magnified throughput impact after slot changes.

Customer communication summary:
- 18:15: Acknowledged receipt; asked for request IDs/examples.
- 18:40: Provided initial engineering update and temporary mitigation (increase pool min-size and enable fallback routing threshold).
- 19:10: Notified customer of recovery and planned root cause investigation; offered incident RCA board meeting.

Notes on related artifacts:
- Slack: #support-quilledge thread (link: slack://channel/support-quilledge/T04XXX)
- Dashboard: rp-west-22 / reserved-pool metrics (link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rp-west-22)
- Postmortem draft page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPPORT/SUP-309271-RCA (internal)

investigation_notes: Repro steps executed in staging replicated PGFAULT spike only when background NVMe IO and many short-stream connections co-occurred. Profiling shows driver page reclamation latency increases under IO pressure. Autoscaler tie-breaker logic uses moving-average attach latency which crossed shrink threshold prematurely. Confirmed KV cache rebuild cost is ~120ms per slot for redwood-instruct-7b-v2 which, multiplied across concurrent slot churn, aligns with observed throughput drop magnitude.
resolution:
Mitigations applied 18:30-19:05: 1) Deployed updated GPU driver micro-patch to reduce page-fault latency on affected nodes. 2) Temporarily increased reserved-pool min-size and disabled immediate shrink windows for rp-west-22. 3) Adjusted autoscaler hysteresis settings to require longer sustained attach failure (cooldown from 90s to 180s) before scale-down in pools with high short-stream mix. 4) Scheduled snapshotter maintenance to avoid co-locating heavy NVMe IO on serving nodes during peak windows.

Permanent follow-ups:
- Engineering to land autoscaler change that factors in KV cache warmup penalty when deciding scale-downs (PR: see related_github_prs).
- Ops to roll driver micro-patch to other clusters where PGFAULTs observed.
- Runbook update to include guidance for noisy snapshotter snapshotting near serving nodes.

Customer impact: Resolved; customer accepted mitigation and requested postmortem meeting. No billing credits requested as fallback routing preserved availability.
